# Vyre, in full

Vyre is the agentic command center for AI-native teams. Our mission is to help every professional services team become AI-native. People and agents share chats, records, tasks, files and automations (Flows) on a server the team owns, and anything that leaves the team waits for a person's yes. Open source (Apache 2.0), self-hosted, any model: Claude, Codex, Grok and OpenRouter through your own subscriptions or keys. Reach it from the Vyre app on a Mac, on Windows, on a phone, or in a browser.

Release 0.5.0. Updated 2026-10-13. Source: https://github.com/vyre-ai/vyre. Licence: Apache 2.0.

## What it is
- People and agents in the same chats. @ a teammate or an agent, # a record, a file or a project. Anyone in the Space can make an agent and share it with a person or a role as use-only or full.
- Agents wake on a task and finish it: the agent ends the task as done, hands it on, or marks it stuck with a plain reason. Each agent and each project has an AGENTS.md instructions file.
- One group chat across providers. Claude, Codex, Grok and OpenRouter answer in the same chat through the sign-ins and keys you add. Give agents different jobs: a team that does the work, one model that reviews, one that plans.
- Flows run the same way every time. A trigger (a person, a schedule with business hours and holidays, a record change, a stage, a form, a link or a watcher), then steps: find, create, update, find-or-create, wait for a time, a date or an event, ask, assign, call a connected service, run an agent. A person approves a Flow before it runs, and each run has its own page.
- Playbooks are project templates: stages, the tasks in each stage, who does each task, and when a stage counts as done. Each kind of work can run as its own track, with its own Playbook and Flows over shared records.
- Records: contacts, projects, tasks and your own record types, with fields in named groups, tags, saved views, Excel or CSV import, and CSV export from the web app. Fields marked sealed show an agent a placeholder, never the value.
- Documents fill your own Word templates from a record and the records linked to it, as Word or PDF. Signing sends a document for signature from a record; the signer needs no account, and the signed copy files back on the record.
- Files: one Files place for the Space, with linked Google Drive and Dropbox folders read through each person's own account.
- The Vault holds passwords, API keys, logins with one-time codes, cards, notes and SSH keys, in groups, shared as Can use or Can edit. Agents use a credential without seeing it.
- Sites: an agent builds a site, previews it at a private address, and puts it live on one yes from you.
- Needs you is one place for approvals, asks and stuck tasks. Teams get roles, per-project seat levels and invites with a role.
- Everything that leaves your server (an email, a payment, a deletion, a published page) waits at the Gate for a person to approve the exact words. An agent can ask and cannot approve.
- Architecture: see https://vyre.run/architecture/ and https://vyre.run/docs/project/ARCHITECTURE.
- The four pillars in depth: https://vyre.run/vault/ (sealed credentials, use-only grants, leases), https://vyre.run/records/ (custom types, links, link hops in tokens, sealed fields), https://vyre.run/flows/ (triggers, approved versions, the runner, holds) and https://vyre.run/agents/ (instructions, memory, access, waking on a task).

## Vyre Computer
- Vyre Computer is how an agent uses a browser, a desktop or an app when no cleaner way exists: https://vyre.run/computer/. It tries the site's own interface first and the screen last. Logins are filled by the Vault, so the model never sees a password. Anything that sends, posts or pays waits for a person.
- Vyre for Chrome drives the Chrome you already have open, signed in as you: https://vyre.run/computer/chrome/. It runs two ways. Standalone, it is an MCP server plus a Chrome extension for Claude Code with no Vyre server (command: vyre-chrome; build it from https://github.com/vyre-ai/vyre/tree/main/local/hands-chrome-mac/standalone). Native, it is the same code inside Vyre on a Mac, where a held send becomes a card in Needs you. The Vault fill extension (modules/vault-extension) fills logins, passkeys and one-time codes from your Vault in Chrome, Arc, Edge, Brave and Firefox.
- How Chrome control works is written as an engineering document at https://vyre.run/computer/architecture/: a read is tried through the site's own API call (learned from the page's traffic, called from inside the page with your login); the page is the fallback; DevTools and a screenshot come after. It remembers each site's structure (never a value) and reuses it. An agent posts its plan first. A send, post or payment is held and re-checked against the page before it goes. Esc stops everything. Every session writes a masked local log.
- Computer use today: one front door (computer.use) over your Chrome, your Mac (through the accessibility tree) and a computer of each agent's own on your server (a desktop, Chrome and a terminal, with a home folder that survives restarts); a Vault sign-in the agent never sees; take-over by a person; a computer you lend to a Space runs its sessions in a sandbox with an encrypted workspace.
- Next (direction, not dates): one Chrome extension that signs in like a device of yours (0.5.2), Chrome control for chats (0.5.2), a chat in the browser side panel (0.5.2), Screen Share on every device, driving a connected computer from your phone, agents borrowing a computer from the Space's pool, and a Chrome profile per agent.

## Vyre by kind of firm (pages under https://vyre.run/for/)

Each page follows one client from inquiry to closed work for an invented firm, and names the Vyre pieces behind every step. The firms and the sample data are invented.

### Law firms: https://vyre.run/for/law-firms/
1. Inquiry comes in
2. Screening and conflict check
3. Consultation
4. Engagement letter signed
5. Matter opens from a Playbook
6. Deadlines from a trigger date
7. Documents and client updates
8. Closing and billing hand-off
Tracks (Playbooks): Personal injury, Estate plan. Agents: Intake, Drafting, Reviewer, Updates. Apps named: Clio, Lawmatics, Practice tools, Zoho, RingCentral, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Dropbox, DocuSign.

Today: a Connection plus a Flow service step, or a custom module. Next, 0.5.2: packaged Integrations (Clio, Lawmatics, GoHighLevel and DecisionVault are the first planned).

## Where it runs
- Server: Linux with Docker Compose 2.24 or newer, or a Mac that stays on. Installed in /srv/vyre by one line, curl -fsSL vyre.run/i | sh, which the Vyre app shows. Images are pulled by digest after their signatures are checked. Updates are signed with a pinned key; a box refuses unsigned, tampered or older releases. Stable never takes a prerelease.
- Mac: the Vyre app in its own window, from the GitHub release (Vyre-aarch64.dmg or Vyre-x86_64.dmg). Not yet signed with an Apple Developer ID, so it opens once with Open Anyway. Needs macOS 14 or newer.
- Windows: Vyre, a tray app with an Alt+Space panel, installed with VyreSetup.exe from the GitHub release. Not Authenticode-signed yet, so Windows asks for "More info", then "Run anyway". Pairs with 13 words or a QR code. The server does not run on Windows yet.
- Phone: the Vyre app, sideloaded (the Android APK from the release, or an iPhone build installed with Xcode), paired by scanning a code, with Face ID or a fingerprint. A removed phone wipes itself.
- Network: built in. Nothing to install or sign in to; the relay carries a connection when a direct path is not possible.

## Install
1. Reserve your name at https://vyre.run/setup/ and copy the code it shows.
2. Install the app from https://github.com/vyre-ai/vyre/releases/latest: Vyre-aarch64.dmg or Vyre-x86_64.dmg on a Mac, VyreSetup.exe on Windows. Both are sideloaded (not signed with a store identity yet).
3. Open the app, paste the code and save the recovery code.
4. Choose Join a team, Add a server (a Linux machine, or a Mac that stays on; With Records is recommended) or, on a Mac, Use My Home.
5. To add a server, run the one line the app shows on it, as yourself: `curl -fsSL https://vyre.run/i | VYRE_CODE=<code from the app> sh`. Confirm the four words in the app.
6. Add your phone from the app: Vyre-android.apk from the release on Android (sideloaded); iPhone has no App Store app yet.

## What it costs
Vyre is free and open source. You pay your AI providers (Claude, Codex, Grok, OpenRouter) on your own subscriptions or keys. Your data lives on your devices and on servers you or your team run. Vyre doesn't hold it.

## Where your data lives
Records, chats, files and the vault stay on your server and your computers. vyre.run holds your name's DNS record and runs the relay (relay.vyre.run), which carries phone pairing, end-to-end encrypted. Prompts go to your AI provider the way they would from that provider's own app.

## Releases
- 0.5.0 (out now): people and agents in the same chats, Flows, Playbooks, Records, a Vault for people and agents, Sites, Documents and Signing.

## How Vyre compares
Each page below describes approaches. About another product it says only what that product’s own public documentation says, and otherwise it describes the kind of tool. Vyre can be extended by integrating your Zoho, QuickBooks, RingCentral and the rest of your software stack*. *Where the vendor provides an API. Packaged Integrations are Next, in 0.5.2.

### Vyre and automation tools: Zapier, Make and n8n (https://vyre.run/compare/automation-tools/)
Zapier, Make and n8n connect apps. Vyre keeps the work, the people and the agents in one place and runs Flows over them. The two fit together well, and this page shows where each is the better tool.
- Who automation tools are for: Zapier, Make and n8n are workflow automation tools. A trigger in one app starts actions in others. They suit operations, marketing and technical teams that want to link the apps they already use, often without writing code.
- What they do well: A large catalogue of app connections. Each of the three offers a wide library of ready-made connections to other products. Fast for a single link. One trigger and one action can be running in minutes. Visual builders. People who do not write code build and read automations on a canvas. Run history. Each shows what ran and what failed, and teams that run them every day know how to read it. Choice of hosting. Zapier and Make are hosted services. n8n can also be run on your own server.
- Where Vyre is different: Flows start from your work. A Flow can start when a record is created or changes, when a record enters a stage, on a schedule, from a form, or when something new arrives in a mailbox or folder. A person approves a version. Editing a Flow makes a new version. A person approves it before it runs, and a saved test that fails blocks the approval. You can go back to an earlier version. Judgment is one step you place. A Flow follows its steps the same way each run. When a step needs judgment, you hand it to an agent, which finishes the task, hands it on, or marks it stuck with a reason. Sends wait at the Gate. A Flow that emails a customer holds the message until a person has read the exact words and approved them. An approved Flow version can carry one yes for named destinations and limits. The Flow has the approver’s reach. A Flow runs with no more authority than the person who approved it, and every step is checked the way a person’s own action is. Credentials stay sealed. A Flow or an agent uses a login from the Vault. The value is put in at the moment of sending and a model never sees it.
- How they work together: Keep the automations that work. A Zap, scenario or workflow can call a Vyre Flow’s path when something happens in an app, and the Flow takes over with the records, the agents and the Gate. A Flow’s web step can call an automation tool’s webhook when you want its connection to an app Vyre does not yet package. A useful split: let the automation tool carry data between apps, and let Vyre decide what the team does with it and who says yes.
- Comparison:
  - Where it runs. Automation tools: Zapier and Make are hosted by the vendor. n8n is hosted or self-hosted. Vyre: On a server you own.
  - What starts work. Automation tools: A trigger in a connected app. Vyre: A person, a schedule, a record change or stage, a form or inbound call, or something new in a mailbox or folder.
  - What it works on. Automation tools: Data passed from one app to another. Vyre: Records, tasks and files kept in the same place as the Flow.
  - Judgment steps. Automation tools: Many include AI steps. Vyre: An agent step you place on purpose. A task it cannot finish is marked stuck, with a reason.
  - Changing a live automation. Automation tools: Set by each tool. Vyre: An edit is a new version. A person approves it, and an earlier version can be restored.
  - Outward actions. Automation tools: Set by how each automation is built. Vyre: Held at the Gate until a person approves the exact words.
  - Credentials. Automation tools: Held in each tool’s own connection store. Vyre: The Vault. Agents get use only and never read the value.
  - Ready-made app connections. Automation tools: A large catalogue. Vyre: A connection to any service that has an API, used from a Flow’s web step. Next (0.5.2): packaged Integrations.
  - Cost. Automation tools: Set by each vendor. Vyre: Vyre is free and open source (Apache 2.0). You pay your AI providers directly.

### Vyre and work management tools: Notion, ClickUp, Asana, Monday (https://vyre.run/compare/work-management/)
Notion, ClickUp, Asana and Monday help a team plan and track work. Vyre adds agents that take tasks, a Gate on what leaves, and a server you own. Many teams will use both.
- Who work management are for: Notion, ClickUp, Asana and Monday are hosted workspaces for planning and tracking work. They hold tasks, boards, timelines, documents and dashboards. They suit teams that want one shared place to see who is doing what and when.
- What they do well: Views people already know. Boards, lists, calendars and timelines, refined over many years. Templates and a familiar interface. A new teammate or an outside client often knows the tool already. Docs and wikis next to tasks. Notion in particular puts pages, databases and notes in one workspace. Reporting dashboards. Portfolio and workload views for managers. A large ecosystem. Integrations, templates and a community of people who can help.
- Where Vyre is different: Agents are members. An agent has a job, instructions in its own AGENTS.md, the projects it can reach and a share of the Vault. A task assigned to it wakes it. It finishes the task, hands it on, or marks it stuck. Records of any shape. Beside tasks, a Space holds contacts, organizations, projects and record types you define, linked in any web, with boards by stage, calendars and dashboards. Playbooks run each kind of work. A Playbook lists the stages and tasks of one kind of job and who does each: a person, a role or an agent. It goes live when an owner approves it. Flows between the stages. Where a Playbook sets the stages, a Flow does the actions between them, and a person approves each version. Sends wait at the Gate. An agent that finishes a task cannot email the client on its own. The Gate holds the message until a person approves it. Your data on your server. Records, files and history are kept on a server you own. Sealed fields show an agent a placeholder.
- How they work together: Keep the board your team already reads. Where the vendor provides an API or an MCP server, a connection lets a Flow read or update it, and a person can add the MCP server for agents to use. Vyre then holds the records, the agent work and the approvals, and the planning tool shows the status. Teams that want one place for everything can run the work in Vyre alone: tasks, Playbooks and boards by stage are all there.
- Comparison:
  - Where it runs. Work management: Hosted by the vendor. Vyre: On a server you own.
  - Unit of work. Work management: Tasks, items, pages and databases. Vyre: Tasks, plus records of any type you define, linked to each other.
  - Who does the work. Work management: People. Most of these tools now include AI features that help inside the tool. Vyre: People and agents, both as members. An agent takes a task, then finishes, hands on or marks it stuck.
  - Process. Work management: Project and board templates. Vyre: Playbooks: stages, tasks and who does each. An owner approves one before it goes live.
  - Automation. Work management: Built-in rules and automations. Vyre: Flows: stored steps, a person approves each version, every run follows it.
  - Views. Work management: Boards, lists, calendars, timelines and dashboards. Vyre: Boards by stage, calendars by date and dashboards over any record type.
  - Documents. Work management: Pages and docs inside the tool. Vyre: Your own Word templates filled from records, with signing for people who have no account.
  - Outward actions. Work management: Set by how each automation is built. Vyre: Held at the Gate until a person approves the exact words.
  - Sensitive fields. Work management: The tool’s own permission settings. Vyre: Sealed fields show an agent a placeholder, and fields can be hidden from named roles.

### Vyre and AI assistants: team workspaces and agent platforms (https://vyre.run/compare/ai-assistants/)
A team AI workspace gives people a strong assistant from one vendor. Vyre gives a team and its agents a shared place to work, on any model, with a person’s yes before anything leaves. Vyre uses these assistants as its models.
- Who ai assistants and agent platforms are for: Team workspaces such as ChatGPT team plans and Claude for teams give each person a hosted assistant from one vendor, with shared projects and connections to common apps. Agent builders let a developer define an agent with instructions and tools and run it on the vendor’s platform.
- What they do well: The vendor’s newest models and features. The people who build the model also build the assistant around it. Nothing to run. You sign up, invite the team and start. The vendor operates it. Polished apps. Chat apps on the web, desktop and phone, with admin controls for the organisation. Connections to common apps. Connectors let an assistant read from and act in products your team already uses. Agent builders for custom agents. A developer can wire tools and instructions into an agent without hosting the model.
- Where Vyre is different: Any model, one chat. Claude, Codex, Grok and OpenRouter answer in the same chat through your own accounts or keys. Changing provider mid-conversation does not lose the conversation. Agents have a role and a reach. Each agent has its own job, instructions and the projects it can reach. What it may do is never more than the person who started it. The work lives beside the chat. Records, tasks, files and Flows sit in the same Space as the conversation, so an agent works on the real thing. Sessions on your own computer. A session can run on a person’s own computer, in a sandbox with an encrypted workspace, or on the server. The chat shows which. Sends wait at the Gate. An agent can ask to send. A person approves the exact words with a proof made on their own device. Credentials stay out of the model. A model sees a placeholder. The real value goes in at the moment of sending, outside the model.
- How they work together: Keep the assistants. Vyre signs in to your own provider accounts and uses them as the models for its agents, so the team keeps the vendor’s models and adds a shared place to work. An outside AI tool connected over MCP can ask Vyre to do work, and the call is checked like any other. Use the assistant for the thinking and Vyre for the work: the records it reads, the Flow it runs and the yes that lets the result out.
- Comparison:
  - Where it runs. AI assistants and agent platforms: The vendor’s cloud. Vyre: A server you own. Sessions run there or on a person’s own computer.
  - Models. AI assistants and agent platforms: The vendor’s own models. Vyre: Claude, Codex, Grok and OpenRouter, through your own accounts or keys.
  - Shared work. AI assistants and agent platforms: Shared workspaces for chats and files. Vyre: Records, tasks, files and Flows in the same Space as the chats.
  - Who can act. AI assistants and agent platforms: A person prompts. Connectors and agents act inside the product. Vyre: People and agents are members with a role and a reach. An agent has no more authority than the person who started it.
  - Repeatable processes. AI assistants and agent platforms: Saved instructions and prompts. Agent builders define workflows in code or configuration. Vyre: Flows: stored steps, a person approves each version, every run follows it.
  - Outward actions. AI assistants and agent platforms: Set by each product’s connectors and permissions. Vyre: Held at the Gate until a person approves the exact words.
  - Credentials. AI assistants and agent platforms: Connectors sign in with an account. Vyre: The Vault. Agents get use only and never read the value.
  - Getting started. AI assistants and agent platforms: Sign up and invite people. Vyre: Set up a server you own, then pair the Vyre app.

### Vyre with practice software and CRMs: Clio, Karbon, HubSpot (https://vyre.run/compare/practice-software/)
Practice management and CRM suites are built for one job and do it well. Vyre does not replace them. It adds a working layer beside them, where people and agents do the intake, drafting, follow-up and review, with a yes before anything goes out.
- Who practice software and crm suites are for: Clio is practice management for law firms. Karbon is practice management for accounting firms. HubSpot is a CRM with marketing and sales tools. Each is a hosted system built for its field. They suit firms and teams that want one dependable record of clients, work and communication.
- What they do well: Built for one profession or function. The record types, terms and screens match how the field works. A system of record. Clients, work, communication and history sit in one dependable place that the whole firm uses. Established ecosystems. Each has partners, integrations and people who know it well. Years of fit with daily practice. They reflect how firms in that field actually run their day. Vendor support and a hosted service. The vendor runs it, updates it and answers questions.
- Where Vyre is different: A working layer, not a replacement. Vyre does not aim to replace your billing or your system of record. It holds the working records and the agent work around them. Agents do the preparation. An agent can read a new enquiry, draft a reply from your price list or fill a document, and then stop for a person. Documents from your templates. Your own Word templates are filled from a record and its linked records, and a model does not retype them. Signing needs no account for the signer. Sends wait at the Gate. Anything that goes to a client, a payment or a deletion waits until a person has read the exact words and approved them. Your server holds the working data. Records, files and the history of every decision stay on a server you own. Sealed fields keep the most sensitive values away from agents. Shaped to your business. Define record types and fields in your own words, link them, and give each kind of work its own Playbook and Flows.
- How they work together: Vyre can be extended by integrating your Zoho, QuickBooks, RingCentral and the rest of your software stack*, and the same goes for Clio, Karbon and HubSpot. The suite stays the system of record. Vyre reads from it, does the preparation, and writes back once a person has said yes. *Where the vendor provides an API. Integrations as packaged modules are Next, in 0.5.2. Today a person adds a connection and a Flow uses it from a web step, or a custom module wraps the service.
- Comparison:
  - What it is for. Practice software and CRM suites: Clio: legal practice management. Karbon: accounting practice management. HubSpot: CRM, marketing and sales. Vyre: A shared working layer for people and agents, with records you shape, Flows, Documents and Signing, Sites and a Gate.
  - Where it runs. Practice software and CRM suites: Hosted by the vendor. Vyre: On a server you own.
  - Specialised to a profession. Practice software and CRM suites: Yes, to the field each was built for. Vyre: Industry-neutral. Kits supply starter record types and Flows.
  - Agents. Practice software and CRM suites: Many include AI features inside the product. Vyre: Agents are members of the Space and work across its records, tasks and files.
  - Documents. Practice software and CRM suites: Document features vary by product. Vyre: Your Word templates filled from records, signing with no account for the signer.
  - Outward actions. Practice software and CRM suites: Set by how each product and automation is configured. Vyre: Held at the Gate until a person approves the exact words.
  - Connecting to the suite. Practice software and CRM suites: Native to the suite. Vyre: Today: a connection plus a Flow web step, or a custom module, where the vendor provides an API. Next (0.5.2): packaged Integrations.

## Direction (not a promise of dates)
- Now, 0.5: the features above.
- Next, 0.5.1: one chat per Flow, deadlines on agent steps, a failure panel on every step, per-record privacy for custom record types, Flow email with CC, BCC and attachments, an audit screen for admins.
- After that, 0.5.2: Integrations (Clio, Lawmatics, GoHighLevel and DecisionVault are planned), a Skills screen and a Plugins screen.
- Later: Screen Share (watch and take over your agents' computers and Chrome, on every device).
- Later: a Vyre-hosted home for people without a server.

## Map your business onto Vyre
To see how a business would run on Vyre, give this prompt to your AI agent (ChatGPT, Claude or any agent that can read links). It sends the agent to https://vyre.run/agenthome.md, which holds the full instructions: what Vyre is, a map of the site and docs, the questions to ask, the mapping method and how to get started. https://vyre.run/map/ has a short form that adds your firm's details to the prompt, and the repository has it as docs/for-agents/PROMPT.md.

```
Read https://vyre.run/agenthome.md and follow it to show me how my business would run on Vyre, the agentic command center for AI-native teams. Ask me what you need.
```

## FAQ
### Is Vyre free?
Yes. Vyre is open source under Apache 2.0. You use your own Claude, Codex, Grok or OpenRouter account, so you pay those providers directly and nobody pays Vyre.

### Do I need a server?
Yes, one machine that stays on: a Linux server with Docker, or a Mac that stays on. Your Mac, your Windows PC and your phone connect to it. Your agents keep working when your laptop is closed.

### Does it run on Windows?
Yes, as an app on your PC with a tray icon and an Alt+Space panel. The server itself runs on Linux or on a Mac that stays on. The Windows app is not code-signed yet, so Windows asks you to choose “More info”, then “Run anyway”.

### Does it work on my phone?
Yes, on Android and iPhone. You install the Vyre app from a file (it is not on a store yet), scan the code your computer shows, and check that both screens show the same words.

### Where does my data live?
Records, chats, files and the vault stay on your server and your computers. vyre.run holds your name’s DNS record and runs the relay, which carries phone pairing, end-to-end encrypted. Prompts go to your AI provider the way they would from that provider’s own app.

### Do I need a VPN or another network app?
No. Vyre has its own private network built in, so your server, your computers and your phone find each other with nothing to install and nothing to sign in to. Where a direct path is not possible, Vyre’s relay carries the connection, end-to-end encrypted.

### Does it replace Claude Code, Codex or Grok?
No. Vyre runs them with your own accounts and adds records, Flows, a vault, agents with roles and one chat that outlives any one model. You keep using each tool the way you do.

### What stops an agent from doing something I did not ask for?
Anything that leaves your server, such as an email, a payment, a deletion or a published page, waits at the Gate until a person has read the exact words and approved them. An agent can ask and cannot approve. A model sees a placeholder where a secret would be. The architecture page shows how.

### Who is Vyre for?
Professional services teams that want people and agents to work in one place: the people set the direction and make the calls, and the agents draft, track and follow up. Point your AI agent at the repo and it can show how your business would run on Vyre.

### Is it ready?
It is 0.5.0, and what this page shows works today. What comes next is labelled with its version on the direction page and in the roadmap.
